correctness.rationale: The exact positive factor connecting the nonlinear drift to an odd scalar equilibrium function is reconstructed. Uniform exponential bounds exclude roots on separated intervals; strict convexity gives exactly one unstable root near the confidence-crossing point; strict decrease gives exactly one attracting root exponentially near the extremal opinion; oddness gives all five. Inward vector field and scalar monotonicity determine global basins. Direct exact logarithmic equilibrium identities give the stated O(1/gamma^2) and exponential remainder estimates. The included pure-Decimal checker ran successfully at six different fixed parameter pairs; no finite sample is represented as proof.

value.rationale: The count and explicit finite-steepness basins are a complete, natural small-system equilibrium classification, not an arbitrary computed slice. They rigorously exhibit coexistence of stable compromise and polarization in the same smooth-confidence model and quantify the sharp basin-selection threshold sqrt(delta)-1 plus its finite-steepness displacement. This is directly motivated by the source’s general conjecture that hard-confidence equilibrium patterns admit steep-sigmoid lifts, without claiming a general solution or a paper-sized contribution.
